summary: Submitted residual-frontier research feedback (action=research) with two new SourceRanges (S-api-restore-doc, api.go:1042-1055; S-api-restore-noop, api.go:1080-1099). It records that the supporting paths read this turn hold no further contract discrepancy: randomTimeout and the backoff helpers match their documented bounds, blocking observers are an explicit documented opt-in, the peers.json readers validate the ingested configuration, the discard store returns the documented errors, FileSnapshotStore.Open verifies the stored CRC64 before returning the reader, NewRaft reads the last log before restoring the snapshot with its configuration scan starting above the snapshot index, and the FSM apply paths advance their index consistently for commands and stored configurations. One reporting ambiguity is preserved as an unresolved question rather than a defect: Raft.Restore applies a no-op after the restore completes and returns that future's error, so a leadership loss or enqueue timeout that prevents the no-op from committing is reported the same way as a failed restore even though the FSM state was already replaced and the burned index advanced; the docs' 'until the restore is complete or an error occurs' does not distinguish the two, while the error is also how the caller learns the new state has not propagated. Remaining work is listed explicitly: that restore-reporting question, the unread peripheral areas (net/tcp transport encoding and version negotiation, FSM batch manager, NewRaft startup reconstruction, testing helpers), and the constructed-environment limits on the five confirmed checks. No map change is proposed because nothing in the accepted map is contradicted. Preflight returned valid:true.
